sections.title: Compound Predicates — AND, OR, NOT, Precedence

blocks.md: **AND before OR — always. Parentheses are documentation that the optimizer respects. Write (A AND B) OR C, not A AND B OR C.**

blocks.label: boolean logic
blocks.py-pandas:
# Parentheses for precedence
e = employees[
    ((employees['salary'] > 50000) & (employees['dept_id'] == 1)) |
    ((employees['salary'] > 60000) & (employees['dept_id'] == 2))
]

# NOT
e = employees[~((employees['dept_id'] == 3) | (employees['salary'] < 30000))]
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Parentheses
from sqlalchemy import or_, and_
session.query(Employee).filter(
    or_(
        and_(Employee.salary > 50000, Employee.dept_id == 1),
        and_(Employee.salary > 60000, Employee.dept_id == 2)
    )
).all()

# NOT
session.query(Employee).filter(
    ~or_(Employee.dept_id == 3, Employee.salary < 30000)
).all()

items.q: NOT A AND NOT B is equivalent to:
items.explain: De Morgan: NOT A AND NOT B = NOT (A OR B).

items.q: x > 5 AND y > 5 OR z > 5 with x=10,y=1,z=10 returns:
items.explain: (x>5 AND y>5) = FALSE; FALSE OR (z>5=TRUE) = TRUE.

sections.title: Subquery IN / EXISTS — The NULL Trap

blocks.label: in with subquery
blocks.mysql: -- MySQL: NOT IN (subquery) also has NULL trap
blocks.py-pandas:
# IN subquery
nyc_depts = departments[departments['location'] == 'NYC']['id']
e = employees[employees['dept_id'].isin(nyc_depts)]

# NOT IN - watch for NaN!
nyc_depts = departments[departments['location'] == 'NYC']['id'].dropna()
e = employees[~employees['dept_id'].isin(nyc_depts)]

# Anti-join (NOT EXISTS equivalent)
merged = employees.merge(departments[departments['location']=='NYC'][['id']], 
                         left_on='dept_id', right_on='id', how='left', indicator=True)
e = merged[merged['_merge'] == 'left_only']

blocks.md: **NOT IN + subquery with NULL = zero rows.** The predicate becomes UNKNOWN for every row. Always use NOT EXISTS or filter NULLs from subquery. This is a classic interview gotcha.

items.q: Subquery returns (1, 2, NULL). WHERE x IN (subquery) with x=1 returns:
items.explain: x=1 matches 1 in list → TRUE. NULL in list doesn't affect positive match.

items.q: Same subquery. WHERE x NOT IN (subquery) with x=5 returns:
items.explain: x=5 not equal to 1, not equal to 2, but '5 <> NULL' is UNKNOWN → whole NOT IN is UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Advanced CASE — Expression, Nesting, Pivot Prep

blocks.label: searched case patterns
blocks.code:
-- Multiple conditions, first match wins
SELECT name, salary,
  CASE
    WHEN salary >= 100000 AND dept_id = 1 THEN 'Eng Senior'
    WHEN salary >= 100000 THEN 'Senior'
    WHEN salary >= 70000 THEN 'Mid'
    ELSE 'Junior'
  END AS level
FROM employees;

-- CASE in WHERE (filter by derived category)
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT *, 
    CASE WHEN salary >= 100000 THEN 'high' ELSE 'normal' END AS pay_band
  FROM employees
) t WHERE pay_band = 'high';

-- CASE in ORDER BY (custom sort)
SELECT * FROM employees
ORDER BY 
  CASE status WHEN 'active' THEN 1 WHEN 'pending' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END,
  salary DESC;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Multiple conditions
conditions = [
    (e['salary'] >= 100000) & (e['dept_id'] == 1),
    (e['salary'] >= 100000),
    (e['salary'] >= 70000)
]
choices = ['Eng Senior', 'Senior', 'Mid']
e['level'] = np.select(conditions, choices, default='Junior')

# Custom sort
e['status_rank'] = e['status'].map({'active': 1, 'pending': 2}).fillna(3)
e = e.sort_values(['status_rank', 'salary'], ascending=[True, False])
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# CASE in ORDER BY
from sqlalchemy import case
session.query(Employee).order_by(
    case(
        (Employee.status == 'active', 1),
        (Employee.status == 'pending', 2),
        else_=3
    ),
    Employee.salary.desc()
).all()

blocks.label: conditional aggregation (pivot prep)
blocks.code:
-- Count by status per department
SELECT dept_id,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active') AS active_cnt,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'pending') AS pending_cnt,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'inactive') AS inactive_cnt
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id;

-- Same with CASE (portable)
SELECT dept_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_cnt,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'pending' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pending_cnt,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'inactive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inactive_cnt
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept_id;
blocks.pg:
-- FILTER clause (PostgreSQL) — cleaner, index-friendly
SELECT dept_id,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active') AS active_cnt
FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id;
blocks.mysql:
-- No FILTER; use CASE
SELECT dept_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_cnt
FROM employees GROUP BY dept_id;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Pivot table
e.pivot_table(index='dept_id', columns='status', values='id', aggfunc='count', fill_value=0)

items.explain: FILTER is PostgreSQL syntactic sugar; both produce same count.

revisionCard: Precedence: NOT > AND > OR. Parenthesize: (A AND B) OR C
De Morgan: NOT (A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B; NOT (A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B
NOT IN (subquery) + NULL = zero rows. Use NOT EXISTS or filter NULLs
EXISTS stops at first match; IN scans all. EXISTS often faster for NOT
CASE: first WHEN wins; use in SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY
FILTER (PostgreSQL) = portable CASE SUM for conditional aggregation

glossary.def: AND stops at first FALSE; OR stops at first TRUE. ORDER BY CASE leverages this.
NOT EXISTS pattern — returns rows with no match in subquery.
EXISTS / IN pattern — returns rows with at least one match; stops at first.
TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN. WHERE keeps TRUE only; CHECK constraint rejects FALSE only.
CASE inside SUM/COUNT to pivot rows into columns per group.
PostgreSQL: aggregate FILTER (WHERE cond) — cleaner than CASE, index-friendly.
